pattern.description: The opening title drifts sideways while blurring and fading out; the hexagon host diagram blurs and fades in underneath it, settling with a slight scale-down, the top red hex dropping in from above.
pattern.why_premium: Using depth-of-field blur instead of a hard cut keeps the change soft and continuous, so the scene moves from a statement to the product metaphor without a jarring break.

build_hint.gsap: tl.to('.title', {x: 60, filter: 'blur(12px)', opacity: 0, duration: 0.25, ease: 'power2.in'}); tl.fromTo('.hex-cluster', {scale: 1.08, filter: 'blur(14px)', opacity: 0}, {scale: 1, filter: 'blur(0px)', opacity: 1, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power3.out'}, '<0.05'); tl.fromTo('.hex-top', {y: -40, filter: 'blur(14px)', opacity: 0}, {y: 0, filter: 'blur(0px)', opacity: 1, duration: 0.4, ease: 'power3.out'}, '<'); tl.from('.hex-id', {opacity: 0, duration: 0.3}, '-=0.2')
build_hint.remotion: title: interpolate(frame,[0,8],[0,1]) drives translateX 0->60, blur 0->12px, opacity 1->0 (Easing.in(Easing.quad)); cluster: spring({frame: frame-2, fps, config:{damping: 26, stiffness: 160, mass: 1}}) drives scale 1.08->1, blur 14->0px, opacity 0->1; top hex uses the same spring for translateY -40->0.

notes: Burst is short (0.2 s) and mostly blur; the top red hex has no whole-hex candidate box, so b06 (a chip inside it) stands in for it. Exact title direction looks rightward from the filmstrip but is subtle.
